article.name: Archiver RAG
article.summary: Archiver RAG is a local memory layer built around an Obsidian Markdown vault, a persistent Chroma vector index, a file watcher, and MCP tools for search and vault operations. This is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

contact.note: No contact email is published in the official pinned README or SECURITY.md.

who_what.text: The repository is maintained under GitHub account FernandoJRR and presents Archiver RAG as a beta self-hosted Python application that connects an Obsidian vault with MCP-compatible clients. The README says it records information selected by a person or agent, not every conversation automatically.

architecture.text: Markdown files are the readable source of record; Chroma is a persistent derived vector index. Ingest stores source path and note metadata with each chunk, prepends a title/folder/tag/link context prefix, and strips the managed Related section before chunking.
The chunker uses 500-word windows with 50-word overlap. The embedder lazily loads all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and the persistent collection obsidian_vault uses cosine distance.

Wikilinks are graph edges. An auto-linker maintains a managed Related section; optional folder descriptions and type metadata can guide placement, while automatic placement, folder description refresh, and inbox routing are disabled by default.

behavior.text: log_note creates a dated Markdown file under a type folder, slugifies the title, and chooses a numeric suffix on collision rather than overwriting. Agent-written and person-written notes share the same file representation.

The watcher indexes creates and edits by removing existing chunks for the source path and adding new chunks. Sync uses integer modification times to decide whether a file is newer than the indexed version; same-second edits may therefore be missed by that comparison.
The CLI deletion path moves notes to .trash, sweeps inbound managed links, and prunes orphaned chunks. The source note remains recoverable, so this is soft deletion rather than verified erasure.

Search embeds the query, retrieves nearest Chroma chunks, filters by optional type before querying and tags after querying, discards candidates below a 0.35 default score floor, and reranks by direct wikilinks and inbound-link hub count. Results include chunk text, source path, metadata, and score components.
The documented HTTP MCP transport has no built-in authentication or TLS. It binds to loopback by default; an exposed instance relies on a proxy, tunnel, or private network to add access control.

metrics.evidence: The search path includes a semantic score floor and graph reranking. No answer-quality or abstention probes were run.
Markdown edits reindex a note, but the inspected design has no semantic correction history. No correction probes were run.
The CLI moves notes to recoverable .trash and prunes their active index chunks. No post-delete probes or copy audits were run.
The reviewed path scopes to a configured vault and optional type/tag filters; it has no principal or tenant access predicate. No isolation probes were run.
Results include retrieved text and source path, but the MCP response has no claim-level citation contract. No response adjudication was run.
Embedding, Chroma retrieval, reranking, and watcher indexing are source-visible. No timings were collected for this review.
The project documents local model/install sizes and persistent Chroma storage, but no token, cost, or corpus-attributed storage measurements were collected for this review.

limits.text: This bounded source review does not measure retrieval quality, threshold calibration, watcher behavior under live edits, deletion completeness, access isolation, latency, cost, or storage efficiency.

The repository describes the product as beta and lists macOS/Linux support, with Windows unsupported. The MCP HTTP transport has no authentication; deployment safety depends on keeping it local or adding an external access-control layer.
The inspected note/index pipeline is Markdown-oriented. PDF and other document ingestion is described as future work in the README, not as current behavior.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. No Archiver RAG runtime, benchmark workload, build, or tests were run for this review. The review records source observations only.
The project metric definitions and fixture describe planned workload cases; they are not measurements or results for Archiver RAG.
